record.paper_title: Brane Supersymmetry Breaking and the Cosmological Constant: Open Problems
record.original_question: Among candidate non-BPS soliton backgrounds that realize this brane-world scenario, which ones satisfy the consistency condition that the supertrace of the squared bulk supergravity mass matrix vanishes, Str M^2_bulk = 0, so that the induced four-dimensional curvature is not catastrophically too large? Since local supersymmetry does not guarantee this cancellation, the open problem is to compute the full bulk spectrum for each background and determine whether the required vanishing supertrace holds without fine-tuning.

evidence.quote: Even when this is the case, the bulk fields produce a curvature radius of the universe that is too big (of solar system scales), unless Str M2 bulk = 0 .
The question is then, is Str M2 bulk = 0 ?
So Str M2 bulk = 0 is an important consistency criterion that must be checked for each non–BPS soliton background individually.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider brane-world scenarios in which our four-dimensional universe is realized as a non-BPS soliton of a higher-dimensional supergravity theory (with at least two transverse extra dimensions) that breaks all supersymmetries in the brane (matter) sector while leaving supersymmetry locally realized in the bulk. For such a background, let M^2_bulk denote the squared mass matrix of all bulk supergravity fields (graviton, gravitini, gauge fields, scalars, fermions, etc.) computed in the soliton background, and define the bulk supertrace

  Str M^2_bulk = Σ_J (-1)^{2J} (2J+1) Tr M^2_J,

summed over all bulk fields of spin J. Phenomenological viability (in particular, an induced four-dimensional curvature that is not parametrically of solar-system scale) requires the consistency condition

  Str M^2_bulk = 0,

which is not automatically enforced by local bulk supersymmetry once the brane sector breaks all supersymmetries.

Problem: For each candidate non-BPS soliton background realizing such a brane-world scenario, compute the complete bulk Kaluza–Klein spectrum and determine whether the condition Str M^2_bulk = 0 holds without fine-tuning. Classify which backgrounds (if any) satisfy this vanishing supertrace identity.
artifact.status_search_result: The vanishing bulk supertrace Str M^2_bulk = 0 is described as a necessary consistency criterion that must be checked case-by-case for each non-BPS soliton background. Subsequent literature on brane supersymmetry breaking and non-supersymmetric strings (e.g., recent work on the cosmological constant and dark dimensions) continues to treat this cancellation as a constraint to be imposed or examined, rather than as a property derived in general. No definitive resolution applicable to all candidate backgrounds appears to have been established.

status_evidence.title: Brane Supersymmetry Breaking and the Cosmological Constant: Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Str M^2 bulk = 0 is an important consistency criterion that must be checked for each non-BPS soliton background individually.
status_evidence.claim: The vanishing of the bulk supertrace is posed as an open consistency condition to be verified case-by-case.

status_evidence.title: The Cosmological Constant and Dark Dimensions from Non-Supersymmetric Strings
status_evidence.snippet: Recent treatment of cosmological constant in non-supersymmetric string compactifications continues to analyze bulk mass spectra and supertrace constraints.
status_evidence.claim: The condition remains an active topic in non-supersymmetric brane/string constructions.

status_evidence.title: Cosmological constant and kinetic supersymmetry breakdown on a moving brane
status_evidence.snippet: Subsequent work explores related supersymmetry breaking on branes without establishing a general Str M^2_bulk = 0 theorem.
status_evidence.claim: No general resolution of the supertrace condition across all non-BPS backgrounds is reported.
